rule: Lua: module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file (`core.common` for data/core/common.lua; ambiguous matches go to the require root that explains the most requires; ...). Functions on the module's returned table are `mod#fn`
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. The require strings `core.common` and `core.doc` are explained by the require root data/ (both files exist as data/core/common.lua and data/core/doc.lua); the scan root src/ explains none of them. So the modules are `core.common` and `core.doc`, not `data.core.common`/`data.core.doc` (the SPEC's own example). Each file is required by the other (common.lua lazily, inside a function), so neither name depends on an entry-file rule. doc.lua's module-level require has caller `core.doc`.
